transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this trouble when people are talking to me. Like down at the museum, people will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them, but then I realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. I always end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It happens enough that I figured I should come in and see what's going on.
Can you tell me what's going through your mind when people are talking to you during these moments? Are you focused on what they're saying, or do you find your attention drifting to other things?

To be honest, I'm not really sure. It's not like I'm actively thinking about something else, like what I'm having for dinner or anything like that. I try to stay focused on what they're saying, but... my mind just sort of drifts off. I don't really know where it goes. I just suddenly realize I've blanked out, but I couldn't tell you what I was actually thinking about instead.
Have you ever felt like you're hearing things that others don't, or had thoughts that made you feel suspicious of people around you?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear things that aren't there, and I don't feel suspicious of anyone. It's really just the trouble with my mind drifting off when people are talking to me.
Have you ever experienced any strange sensations, like feeling detached from yourself, or found that your thoughts feel disorganized or hard to follow?

No, I can't say I've ever felt detached from myself or anything like that. And my thoughts aren't really disorganized... they just kind of fade out. I don't have any strange sensations, it's just that blanking out thing I mentioned before.
Does this kind of drifting off or trouble staying focused happen in other situations, like when you're reading, working on tasks, or listening to lectures?

Yeah, it definitely happens when I'm reading, too. I can sit down with, say, a gallery packet or some notes, and I usually start out fine. But after just a few minutes... I'll realize my eyes are still moving over the page, but my mind has completely wandered off somewhere else. I always end up having to go back and read the exact same part all over again because I didn't actually take any of it in.
When did you first start noticing this trouble with your mind drifting off or losing focus during conversations or reading?

Well, it's been noticeably causing trouble for about two years and four months now. That's when my friend died, and I ended up taking over the museum liaison duties all by myself. It seems like it really started becoming an issue around then.
Do you find that you're easily distracted by things around you when you're trying to focus on a task, like working on museum reports or anything else that requires your attention?

No, not really. It's not like a noise outside or people talking pulls me away from what I'm doing. It's more like the distraction comes from inside my own head. I just sort of... drift away, even if the room is completely quiet.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down or lose interest in things you usually enjoy, like working at the museum or other activities?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel down, and I still enjoy the museum work and my other activities just as much as I always have. I mean, it gets a little frustrating when I can't keep my mind on what I'm doing, but I haven't lost interest in it or anything. My mood is generally pretty good.
Do you find that you often have trouble finishing tasks, like museum reports or other projects, even if you start them with every intention of completing them?

Yeah, I do. For example, when someone gives me a few things to handle for the volunteer group, I’ll do the first part without a problem, like printing out the maps. But then... I might just forget to call the museum desk, or I'll leave the folders sitting there half-ready. I usually don't finish the rest of it up until someone actually reminds me.
Do you often find yourself forgetting where you put things, like keys or documents, or feel like you're not as organized as you used to be in handling daily responsibilities?

Yeah, I do that a lot. I’m always putting down the camera battery, or the name tags, or... the envelope with the volunteer sign-up sheets. I'll put them somewhere safe, and then I end up spending half the morning just retracing my steps trying to find them again.
Do you often find yourself struggling to stay focused or organized in everyday situations, like following a conversation, keeping track of time, or managing multiple things at once?

I don't think so, no. I mean, I can follow a conversation just fine, and I don't really have trouble keeping track of time. Managing multiple things... I guess I just don't really notice any big issues with that stuff. It's more just the forgetting where I put things and not finishing what I start, like I mentioned.
